verdict: No, a single dump leg at the transfer station does not close the gap: recorded km are about 3x the modeled road distance (median ratio 3.09 with the dump leg, 3.29 without; 0% of runs within +/-30%), and the ~107 km median surplus dwarfs the ~9 km a TS dump adds. The surplus is uncorrelated with distance to the TS (Pearson r=0.02, p=0.66; Spearman r=0.08), morning and afternoon runs look alike, so one facility closure cannot explain the odometer readings. The likely explanation is that sensor-visible stops capture only a fraction of the physical route: bins without sensors, repeated area sweeps and possibly multiple dump trips per shift make km_rec roughly triple the shortest-path model.
